subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: Bagan: Land of Ten Thousand Temples
description: A 60-second lesson on Bagan: Land of Ten Thousand Temples.

hook.text: A plain in Myanmar holds over 2,000 Buddhist temples built in just 250 years. Kings competed to build the most.

buildup.text: Between 1000 and 1300 CE, Bagan's rulers built more than 10,000 temples across 26 square miles.

discovery.text: The Ananda Temple contains four standing Buddhas, each 31 feet tall, facing the four cardinal directions.

twist.text: A Mongol invasion in 1287 ended the building frenzy. Earthquakes later toppled many of the remaining temples.

climax.text: Myanmar's controversial restorations have added concrete to ancient brick, sparking debate among archaeologists.

punchline.text: Ten thousand temples rose in 250 years. Two thousand still stand.

quiz.question: What ended the temple-building era at Bagan?
options: The royal treasury ran out of funds
A Mongol invasion in 1287 ended the building period
Buddhist monks declared that no more temples were needed

details.summary: Bagan in Myanmar contains over 3,500 surviving Buddhist temples, pagodas, and monasteries built between the 9th and 13th centuries. At its peak, over 10,000 religious structures covered the plain. The Bagan kingdom fell to Mongol invasions in 1287, but the temples endured.
details.whyItMatters: Bagan represents one of the greatest concentrations of religious architecture on Earth. Its density of Buddhist monuments across the Irrawaddy plain documents the extraordinary devotion and resources of a medieval Southeast Asian kingdom.
takeaways: Over 3,500 Buddhist temples survive on the Bagan plain
Built between the 9th and 13th centuries by the Bagan kingdom
The kingdom fell to Mongol invasions in 1287

faq.question: Why were so many temples built at Bagan?
faq.answer: Theravada Buddhist kings and wealthy elites built temples to accumulate religious merit. Each ruler tried to surpass his predecessors. The massive construction program diverted resources from military defense, possibly contributing to vulnerability when the Mongols arrived in the late 13th century.

faq.question: What threats do the Bagan temples face today?
faq.answer: A major earthquake in 2016 damaged over 400 temples. Poorly executed restorations using modern materials have altered original structures. Tourism pressure, vegetation growth, and Myanmar's political instability all threaten long-term preservation of this extraordinary site.
